test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 09 Oct, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I cannot call him directly as __I have lost his support.__

options.text: am out of favour with him
am quite at sea with him

solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"am out of favour with him"** means to have lost someone's support or approval. (उसकी कृपा से बाहर होना)

 
 
• **Example: **After the argument, I realized I was out of favour with him.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence is **'am out of favour with him'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **am in my own light** (अपने ही मार्ग में होना): Hindering one's own progress.

 
 
• **Example:** She is in her own light when she doubts her capabilities.
 
 
 
• **am quite at sea with him** (उसके साथ पूरी तरह से भ्रमित होना): To be confused or puzzled about something or someone.
 
 
• **Example: **I am quite at sea with him whenever he talks about his work.
 
 
 
• **am in character** (चरित्र में होना): To act in a way that is typical or expected of someone.
 
 
• **Example:** He is always in character when he performs on stage.
